These describe physiological load. They are not a diagnosis.
Personal ranges need several nights of readings before recovery can use them.

Recovery blends the inputs that are available: heart rate variability (40 percent), resting heart rate (25), sleep (25), breathing rate (5) and skin temperature (5). Your fatigue rating and training load join in when you have them.
Each input is compared with your own last 30 days. A reading at your usual level scores about 50, higher heart rate variability and lower resting heart rate score above that.
If an input is missing, its weight is shared among the others so the score still spans 0 to 100. Heart rate variability or resting heart rate must be present.
67 to 100 is green, 34 to 66 yellow and 0 to 33 red. The score describes how recovered your body looks. It is not medical advice.
